title: Battle of Naissus
description: A Roman army defeats a large Gothic invasion force near Naissus, a turning point in the empire's recovery from the crisis of the third century.

title: Stefan Nemanja becomes grand prince
description: Stefan Nemanja takes power in Serbia and founds the Nemanjić dynasty, which rules for two centuries.

title: Stefan the First-Crowned made king
description: Nemanja's son Stefan receives a crown from Pope Honorius III, making Serbia a kingdom.

title: Serbian Church becomes autocephalous
description: The patriarch in Nicaea consecrates Sava as first archbishop of an independent Serbian church, which he seats at Žiča.

title: Battle of Velbazhd
description: King Stefan Dečanski defeats and kills the Bulgarian tsar Michael Shishman, making Serbia the leading power of the Balkans.

title: Stefan Dušan crowned emperor
description: Dušan is crowned emperor of the Serbs and Greeks on Easter Day, after raising the Serbian archbishop to patriarch, at the height of medieval Serbian power.

title: Dušan's Code
description: A state council enacts a written code of law for the empire, the main legal monument of medieval Serbia.

title: Battle of the Maritsa
description: An Ottoman force surprises and destroys the army of King Vukašin and Despot Uglješa, opening Macedonia to Ottoman conquest.

title: Fall of Smederevo
description: The capital surrenders to Mehmed II, ending the medieval Serbian state and beginning more than three centuries of Ottoman rule.

title: Ottomans take Belgrade
description: Suleiman the Magnificent captures the Hungarian border fortress of Belgrade, which opens the way into the Hungarian plain.

title: Great Migration of the Serbs
description: As the Ottomans retake Serbia from the Habsburgs, Patriarch Arsenije III leads tens of thousands of Serbs north across the Sava and Danube into Habsburg lands.

title: First Serbian Uprising
description: Serbian leaders choose Karađorđe to lead a revolt against the janissary rulers of the Belgrade pashalik, the start of the modern Serbian state.

title: Second Serbian Uprising
description: Miloš Obrenović raises a second revolt, which ends in a negotiated self-government for Serbia under Ottoman suzerainty.

title: Sretenje Constitution
description: An assembly adopts the first Serbian constitution, which limits the prince's power and is suspended within weeks under pressure from the great powers.

title: Kingdom of Serbia proclaimed
description: Four years after independence is recognised at the Congress of Berlin, Prince Milan Obrenović is proclaimed king.

title: May Coup
description: Army officers kill King Alexander Obrenović and Queen Draga and bring the Karađorđević dynasty to the throne, turning Serbia away from Austria-Hungary.

title: Battle of Kumanovo
description: The Serbian army defeats the Ottoman Vardar Army in the First Balkan War, ending Ottoman rule in Macedonia and Kosovo.

title: Battle of Cer
description: The Serbian army throws back the first Austro-Hungarian invasion, the first Allied victory of the First World War.

title: Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes proclaimed
polity: Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes
description: Prince Regent Alexander proclaims the union of Serbia with the South Slav lands of the former Austria-Hungary, the state later named Yugoslavia.

title: King Alexander assassinated
description: A gunman working with the Ustaše and a Macedonian revolutionary organisation shoots the king of Yugoslavia at the start of a state visit to France.

title: Axis invasion of Yugoslavia
description: Germany bombs Belgrade and invades with its allies ten days after a coup against the pact with the Axis, and Yugoslavia is defeated and partitioned within two weeks.

title: Kragujevac massacre
description: German troops shoot more than 2,700 men and boys in reprisal for attacks by insurgents, under an order to kill a hundred hostages for each German soldier killed.

title: Liberation of Belgrade
description: The Red Army and Yugoslav Partisans drive German forces from the city, which becomes the seat of Tito's government.

title: Federal People's Republic proclaimed
description: A constituent assembly abolishes the monarchy and declares Yugoslavia a federal republic of six republics under communist rule.

title: Tito–Stalin split
description: The Cominform, meeting in Bucharest, expels the Yugoslav Communist Party, and Yugoslavia goes on to follow its own course outside the Soviet bloc.

title: First Non-Aligned summit
description: Leaders of 25 states meet at Tito's invitation to found a movement of countries outside the two Cold War blocs.

title: Death of Tito
description: Josip Broz Tito dies after 35 years as leader of Yugoslavia, leaving a rotating collective presidency that cannot contain the disputes between the republics.

title: Gazimestan speech
description: On the 600th anniversary of the Battle of Kosovo, Slobodan Milošević addresses a very large crowd of Serbs in a speech that mentions the possibility of armed battles.

title: NATO bombing of Yugoslavia begins
description: NATO begins 78 days of air strikes to force Yugoslav forces out of Kosovo, which afterwards comes under United Nations administration.

title: Overthrow of Milošević
description: Mass protests over a disputed presidential election storm the federal parliament and Slobodan Milošević concedes defeat.

title: Assassination of Zoran Đinđić
description: The reformist prime minister who had sent Milošević to The Hague is shot by a sniper linked to a special police unit and organised crime.

title: Kosovo declares independence
description: The assembly of Kosovo declares independence from Serbia, which most Western states recognise and Serbia does not.
